title: Sell Mineral Rights in Gillette, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Gillette, WY | PRB Core
metaDescription: Gillette sits in Powder River Basin coal and horizontal oil activity. Get a fair cash offer for your Campbell County mineral interest.
heroLead: Gillette calls itself the Energy Capital of the Nation for a reason. Coal, coalbed methane, and now horizontal oil have all run through Campbell County ground within a single working lifetime.
intro: That layered history means mineral owners around Gillette often hold interests touched by more than one boom. A family that leased for CBM in the early 2000s, watched that play crash, and now finds a horizontal Niobrara or Turner well going in on the same section isn't an unusual story here.

sections.heading: From coalbed methane bust to horizontal oil
paragraphs: The CBM boom peaked in the mid-2000s and collapsed hard when gas prices fell and shallow coal wells stopped penciling. Plenty of Campbell County mineral owners wrote that era off as a wash. Then operators came back with horizontal wells targeting the Niobrara, Turner, Sussex, and Parkman formations thousands of feet deeper, and some of that same ground got leased and drilled again.

sections.heading: Coal royalties are their own animal
paragraphs: Gillette sits atop some of the largest coal reserves in the country, and coal royalty payments run on a different mechanism than oil and gas, tied to surface or federal coal leases and production reports rather than a wellhead meter. If your interest includes coal, keep that royalty stream separate in your mind from any oil and gas minerals on the same land.

sections.heading: Why fractional ownership runs deep here
paragraphs: Decades of drilling, unitization, and family transfers mean a lot of Campbell County minerals sit in small decimal interests spread across siblings, cousins, and trusts. Untangling exactly what you own before selling is often the biggest time cost, more than negotiating the price itself.

faqs.question: I leased for CBM years ago, is that lease still active?
faqs.answer: Many CBM-era leases lapsed when production stopped and weren't renewed. Check your Campbell County Clerk records for the current lease status before assuming you're still under contract.

faqs.question: Do I own coal and oil and gas minerals separately?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, depending on how your deed was written. Some Campbell County deeds separate coal from oil and gas rights entirely; others cover both. A title review clears this up.

faqs.question: How fast does horizontal PRB production decline?
faqs.answer: Faster in the first year or two than legacy vertical wells, then it flattens into a longer stripper-style tail. That curve gets factored into any offer on producing minerals.

faqs.question: Can I sell just my oil and gas minerals and keep coal?
faqs.answer: In many cases yes, if your deed already separates the two, or if a split can be arranged as part of the sale. Talk through your specific deed language before assuming either way.
